questions.text: बीजाण्डावरण कोशिकाओं तथा सहाय कोशिकाओं से विकसित होने वाले असंगजनित भ्रूणों की सूत्रगुणता होगी क्रमशः :
questions.text_english: The ploidy of the apomictic embryos developing from the integument cells and synergids respectively would be :
questions.solution: The correct option is 2n, n. Integument cells are part of the maternal sporophytic tissue and are naturally diploid (2n). Synergids are part of the female gametophyte (embryo sac) and are naturally haploid (n). Therefore, apomictic embryos developing from these cells will possess the corresponding ploidy levels of 2n and n, respectively.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प 2n, n है। बीजाण्डावरण (integument) कोशिकाएँ मातृ बीजाणुउद्भिद (sporophytic) ऊतक का हिस्सा होती हैं और स्वभाव से द्विगुणित (2n) होती हैं। सहाय कोशिकाएँ (synergids) मादा युग्मकोद्भिद (भ्रूण-कोष) का हिस्सा होती हैं और स्वभाव से अगुणित (n) होती हैं। अतः, इनसे विकसित होने वाले असंगजनित भ्रूणों की सूत्रगुणता क्रमशः 2n और n होगी।

questions.text: एक डीएनए खंड में 2500 न्यूक्लियोटाइड्स हैं, जिनमें से 240 ग्वानीन हैं। तो इस डीएनए खंड में दो हाइड्रोजन बंध वाले क्षारों (बेसों) की संख्या कितनी होगी ?
questions.text_english: A DNA fragment has 2500 nucleotides, out of which 240 are Guanine. How many bases having double hydrogen bonds between them does this DNA fragment possess ?
questions.solution: The correct option is 2020. According to Chargaff's rule, the number of Guanine (G) equals Cytosine (C). Since G = 240, C is also 240. The total number of nucleotides forming triple hydrogen bonds (G + C) is 240 + 240 = 480. Out of a total of 2500 nucleotides, the remaining nucleotides are Adenine (A) and Thymine (T), which form double hydrogen bonds. So, the number of bases having double hydrogen bonds is 2500 - 480 = 2020.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प 2020 है। चारगाफ के नियम के अनुसार, ग्वानीन (G) की संख्या साइटोसिन (C) के बराबर होती है। चूंकि G = 240 है, इसलिए C भी 240 होगा। तीन हाइड्रोजन बंध बनाने वाले कुल क्षारों की संख्या (G + C) = 240 + 240 = 480 है। 2500 न्यूक्लियोटाइड्स में से शेष क्षार एडेनिन (A) और थाइमिन (T) होंगे, जो दो हाइड्रोजन बंध बनाते हैं। अतः, दो हाइड्रोजन बंध वाले क्षारों की संख्या 2500 - 480 = 2020 होगी।

questions.text: निषेचन के बिना बीज उत्पन्न करने की प्रणाली का विकास इस कुल के पुष्पी पादपों में हुआ है :
questions.text_english: The mechanism to produce seeds without fertilisation has evolved in the given family of the flowering plants :
questions.solution: The correct option is Asteraceae. The remarkable biological phenomenon of producing seeds without fertilisation is scientifically known as apomixis. This evolutionary mechanism has prominently evolved and is frequently observed in certain flowering plant families, specifically Asteraceae and various species of grasses.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प एस्टेरेसी है। निषेचन के बिना बीज उत्पन्न करने की जैविक घटना को असंगजनन (apomixis) कहा जाता है। यह विकासवादी तंत्र मुख्य रूप से एस्टेरेसी (Asteraceae) कुल के पुष्पी पादपों और घासों की विभिन्न प्रजातियों में विकसित हुआ है।

questions.text: लुई पाश्चर ने स्वतः जनन के सिद्धान्त को अपने प्रयोगों द्वारा खारिज कर दिया । इसके लिए उसने उपयोग किया, पहले से जीवाणुरहित फ्लास्क तथा :
questions.text_english: Louis Pasteur dismissed the theory of spontaneous generation by his experiments using pre-sterilised flasks and :
questions.solution: The correct option is Killed yeast. Louis Pasteur conclusively disproved the deeply rooted theory of spontaneous generation through his famous swan-neck flask experiments. He meticulously demonstrated that life only comes from pre-existing life by showing that in pre-sterilised flasks kept closed to the air, killed yeast did not give rise to new living organisms, whereas when exposed to air, new organisms appeared.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प मृत यीस्ट है। लुई पाश्चर ने अपने प्रसिद्ध स्वान-नेक (हंस-गर्दन) फ्लास्क प्रयोगों के माध्यम से स्वतः जनन के सिद्धांत को निर्णायक रूप से खारिज कर दिया। उन्होंने यह प्रदर्शित किया कि जीवन केवल पूर्व-मौजूद जीवन से ही आता है। उन्होंने दिखाया कि बंद किए गए पहले से जीवाणुरहित फ्लास्कों में मृत यीस्ट से कोई नए जीव उत्पन्न नहीं हुए, जबकि वायु के संपर्क में आने पर नए जीव प्रकट हुए।

questions.text: इंग्लैंड में 1850 के दशक के पश्चात् पश्च-औद्योगीकरण युग में प्राकृतिक वरण के प्रभाव के फलस्वरूप श्वेत पंखों वाले शलभों की संख्या, गहरे (काले) पंखों वाले शलभों की संख्या की अपेक्षा :
questions.text_english: After the 1850s in the post-industrialization era in England, the expected effect of natural selection on the number of white-winged moths as compared to the dark-winged moths was:
questions.solution: The correct option is Less in number. In the post-industrialization era, massive industrial smoke and heavy soot systematically covered the tree trunks, killing the light-coloured lichens and turning the trunks dark. Against this dark background, the white-winged moths completely lost their camouflage and were easily spotted and predated upon by birds. Consequently, natural selection strongly favoured the dark-winged moths, leaving the white-winged moths drastically less in number.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प 'कम थी' है। पश्च-औद्योगीकरण युग में, औद्योगिक धुएं और कालिख ने पेड़ों के तनों को ढक लिया, जिससे हल्के रंग के लाइकेन नष्ट हो गए और तने काले हो गए। इस गहरी पृष्ठभूमि में, श्वेत पंख वाले शलभ अपना छलावरण खो बैठे और पक्षियों द्वारा आसानी से देखे जाने लगे। परिणामस्वरूप, प्राकृतिक वरण ने गहरे पंख वाले शलभों का पक्ष लिया, जिससे श्वेत पंख वाले शलभों की संख्या बहुत कम हो गई।

questions.text: लाल पुष्प वाले स्नेपड्रेगन पौधे का संकरण श्वेत पुष्प वाले स्नेपड्रेगन पौधे के साथ कराया गया । F1 पीढ़ी में प्राप्त संतति का स्वपरागण कराने पर प्राप्त संतति का अनुपात था :
questions.text_english: A Snapdragon plant bearing red colour flowers was crossed with a Snapdragon plant bearing white colour flowers. The F1 progeny on selfing produced the progeny in the ratio of :
questions.solution: The correct option is 25% Red: 50% Pink: 25% White. In Snapdragon (Antirrhinum), flower colour vividly exhibits the phenomenon of incomplete dominance. When a homozygous red flowered plant (RR) is crossed with a homozygous white flowered plant (rr), all F1 offspring uniquely possess a heterozygous (Rr) genotype and produce intermediate pink flowers. When these F1 pink flowers are self-pollinated, the resulting F2 generation sharply segregates into a phenotypic ratio of 1 Red (RR) : 2 Pink (Rr) : 1 White (rr), which translates exactly to 25% Red, 50% Pink, and 25% White.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प 25% लाल : 50% गुलाबी : 25% श्वेत है। स्नेपड्रेगन (Antirrhinum) में पुष्प का रंग अपूर्ण प्रभाविता (incomplete dominance) का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है। जब समयुग्मजी लाल पुष्प (RR) वाले पौधे का समयुग्मजी श्वेत पुष्प (rr) वाले पौधे से संकरण कराया जाता है, तो F1 पीढ़ी में सभी पौधे विषमयुग्मजी (Rr) होते हैं और मध्यवर्ती गुलाबी पुष्प उत्पन्न करते हैं। जब इन F1 गुलाबी पुष्पों का स्वपरागण कराया जाता है, तो F2 पीढ़ी 1 लाल (RR) : 2 गुलाबी (Rr) : 1 श्वेत (rr) के अनुपात में पृथक होती है। यह सटीक रूप से 25% लाल, 50% गुलाबी और 25% श्वेत के बराबर है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित क्रोमोसोमीय विकार में से कौन-से व्यष्टि (व्यक्ति) छोटे कद (बौने), अल्पविकसित स्त्रीवत् लक्षण तथा बंध्य अंडाशय युक्त होते हैं ?
questions.text_english: In which of the following chromosomal disorders do individuals have short stature, underdeveloped feminine character and sterile ovaries ?
questions.solution: The correct option is Turner's syndrome. Turner's syndrome is a significant chromosomal disorder resulting from the complete absence of one of the X chromosomes in females, leading to a karyotype of 45 with X0. Females affected by this disorder prominently exhibit short stature, highly underdeveloped feminine characteristics, and non-functional, rudimentary sterile ovaries.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प टर्नर सिंड्रोम है। टर्नर सिंड्रोम एक प्रमुख गुणसूत्रीय विकार है जो महिलाओं में एक X गुणसूत्र की पूर्ण अनुपस्थिति के कारण होता है, जिससे 45, X0 का कैरियोटाइप बनता है। इस विकार से प्रभावित महिलाओं का कद छोटा होता है, उनमें अल्पविकसित स्त्रीवत् लक्षण दिखाई देते हैं, और उनके अंडाशय निष्क्रिय या बंध्य (sterile) होते हैं।

questions.text: PCR में डीएनए के प्रवर्धन के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा उपक्रामकों के तापानुशीलन को सही प्रकार से निरूपित करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following represents the correct annealing of primers to the DNA to be amplified in the PCR ?

options.A: Primers bind to 5' ends and face away from each other
options.B: Both primers bind to the same end
options.C: Primers bind to 3' ends and grow towards each other
options.D: Primers bind to 5' ends and grow outwards

options_english.A: Primers bind to 5' ends and face away from each other
options_english.B: Both primers bind to the same end
options_english.C: Primers bind to 3' ends and grow towards each other
options_english.D: Primers bind to 5' ends and grow outwards

questions.solution: The correct option is (C). During the critical annealing step of the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), a specific set of short oligonucleotide primers perfectly binds to the complementary sequences located precisely at the 3' ends of both the separated template DNA strands. Because DNA polymerase enzyme strictly extends the new strand from the 5' to the 3' direction, the primers must be fundamentally oriented so their 3' extension ends grow inwards, pointing directly towards each other along the template.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (C) है। पीसीआर (PCR) के तापानुशीलन (annealing) चरण के दौरान, छोटे उपक्रमकों (प्राइमर्स) का एक विशिष्ट सेट पृथक किए गए दोनों डीएनए टेम्पलेट रज्जुकों के 3' सिरों पर जुड़ता है। चूंकि डीएनए पॉलीमरेज़ एंज़ाइम नई श्रृंखला का संश्लेषण हमेशा 5' से 3' दिशा में करता है, प्राइमर्स इस प्रकार जुड़ते हैं कि वे एक-दूसरे की ओर बढ़ते हुए डीएनए का संश्लेषण कर सकें।

questions.text: एक रोगी ज्वर, ठिठुरन, खाँसी, सिरदर्द तथा नीले नाखूनों व होंठों युक्त लक्षणों से पीड़ित है । यह अभिलक्षण दर्शाने वाला रोग है :
questions.text_english: A patient is suffering from fever, chills, cough, headache and bluish finger nails and lips. These symptoms are of the disease :
questions.solution: The correct option is Pneumonia. The prominent clinical symptoms including severe fever, chills, persistent cough, intense headache, and particularly the progression of fingernails and lips turning distinctively bluish due to restricted oxygen supply, are the definitive classic indicators of Pneumonia. This dangerous respiratory infection is frequently caused by pathogens like Streptococcus pneumoniae.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प न्यूमोनिया है। ज्वर, ठिठुरन, लगातार खाँसी, सिरदर्द, और विशेष रूप से ऑक्सीजन की कमी के कारण होंठों और नाखूनों का नीला पड़ जाना न्यूमोनिया (Pneumonia) रोग के स्पष्ट लक्षण हैं। यह श्वसन तंत्र का संक्रमण मुख्य रूप से स्ट्रेप्टोकोकस न्यूमोनी (Streptococcus pneumoniae) नामक जीवाणु के कारण होता है।

questions.text: एक प्रयोग में ई. कोलाई को 14NH4Cl युक्त संवर्धन माध्यम में विकसित किया (14N नाइट्रोजन का हल्का समस्थानिक है) । उसके पश्चात् इसे नाइट्रोजन के भारी समस्थानिक (15N) युक्त संवर्धन माध्यम में 6 पीढ़ियों तक संवर्धित किया गया । 6 पीढ़ियों के बाद उनके डीएनए को निष्कर्षित किया गया तथा CsCl घनत्व प्रवणता पर अपकेन्द्रण द्वारा निष्कर्षित किया गया । CsCl घनत्व प्रवणता अपकेन्द्रण पर डीएनए के सही घनत्व (हल्का/संकरित/भारी) और पट्टियों के अनुपात की पहचान कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: In an experiment, E. coli is grown in a medium containing 14NH4Cl (14N is the light isotope of Nitrogen) followed by growing it for six generations in a medium having heavy isotope of nitrogen (15N). After six generations, their DNA was extracted and subjected to CsCl density gradient centrifugation. Identify the correct density (Light/Hybrid/Heavy) and ratio of the bands of DNA in CsCl density gradient centrifugation.
questions.solution: The correct option is Hybrid: Heavy, 1:31. The bacteria start initially with completely light DNA (14N-14N). When deliberately grown in a medium heavily enriched with a heavy isotope (15N) for precisely 6 generation cycles, the total number of DNA molecules formed equals 2 raised to the power of 6, which is exactly 64 molecules. Because DNA replication is strictly semi-conservative, the 2 original light strands from the first generation serve as templates and ultimately form exactly 2 hybrid DNA molecules (14N-15N). The remaining 62 DNA molecules will be completely heavy (15N-15N). Thus, the exact ratio of Hybrid to Heavy DNA strongly settles at 2:62, which elegantly simplifies down to 1:31.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प संकरित : भारी, 1:31 है। ई. कोलाई में पूरी तरह से हल्का डीएनए (14N-14N) है। भारी समस्थानिक (15N) वाले माध्यम में 6 पीढ़ियों तक वृद्धि करने पर, डीएनए अणुओं की कुल संख्या 2^6 = 64 होगी। अर्धसंरक्षी प्रतिकृतियन के कारण, 2 मूल हल्के रज्जुक केवल 2 संकरित डीएनए (14N-15N) अणु बनाएंगे। शेष 62 डीएनए अणु पूरी तरह से भारी (15N-15N) होंगे। अतः संकरित : भारी का अनुपात 2:62 यानी 1:31 होगा।

questions.text: प्रथम पुनर्योगज डीएनए के प्रतिकृतीयन के लिए, स्टैनले कोहेन तथा हरबर्ट बोयर द्वारा उपयोग किए गए डीएनए पॉलीमरेज़ का स्रोत है :
questions.text_english: For the replication of the first recombinant DNA, Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer used the DNA polymerase of:
questions.solution: The correct option is Escherichia coli. In 1972, Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer successfully constructed the first recombinant DNA by linking an antibiotic resistance gene to a native plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium. However, to achieve massive replication of this newly formed recombinant DNA, they systematically transferred it into a closely related host bacterium, which was Escherichia coli. Therefore, the replication inside the host cell fundamentally utilized the DNA polymerase enzyme naturally belonging to Escherichia coli.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प एशरिकिआ कोलाई है। स्टैनले कोहेन और हरबर्ट बोयर ने 1972 में साल्मोनेला टाइफीमूरियम के प्लाज्मिड में एंटीबायोटिक प्रतिरोध जीन जोड़कर प्रथम पुनर्योगज डीएनए बनाया था। हालांकि, इस डीएनए की प्रतिकृति (replication) के लिए उन्होंने इसे 'एशरिकिआ कोलाई' (E. coli) नामक जीवाणु कोशिका में स्थानांतरित किया था। अतः प्रतिकृतीयन के लिए E. coli के डीएनए पॉलीमरेज़ का ही उपयोग हुआ था।

questions.text: प्रकृति में उगने वाली समष्टि जिसके लिए सीमित संसाधन उपलब्ध हैं, के लिए निरूपित समष्टि वृद्धि वक्र है :
questions.text_english: The population growth curve applicable for a population growing in nature with limited resources available to them will be :
questions.solution: The correct option is (C). In realistic natural habitats, critical resources like food and shelter are always limited. This inherent environmental resistance heavily restricts unrestricted exponential growth. A population actively growing in such a limited resource environment robustly follows the Verhulst-Pearl Logistic growth model, which elegantly yields a classic S-shaped (or Sigmoid) curve on a graph, eventually levelling off completely at the carrying capacity (K).
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (C) है। प्रकृति में, भोजन और स्थान जैसे संसाधन हमेशा सीमित होते हैं, जो समष्टि की अनंत वृद्धि को रोकते हैं। सीमित संसाधनों वाले ऐसे प्राकृतिक वातावरण में बढ़ने वाली समष्टि 'लॉजिस्टिक वृद्धि मॉडल' (Verhulst-Pearl Logistic growth) का पालन करती है। इसे ग्राफ़ पर निरूपित करने पर एक 'S' आकार का वक्र (Sigmoid curve) प्राप्त होता है, जो वहन क्षमता (Carrying capacity) पर पहुँच कर स्थिर हो जाता है।

key_points: A vaccine is a biological preparation containing inactivated or weakened pathogens or antigenic proteins of a pathogen.
It acts on the principle of 'memory' of the immune system.

questions.solution: A vaccine is a carefully formulated biological preparation consisting of specific antigenic proteins of pathogens, or completely inactivated/weakened pathogens themselves, deliberately designed to confer active acquired immunity against a specific disease. Once administered into the body, it acts fundamentally on the sophisticated principle of the immune system's 'memory'. The vaccine mimics a natural infection without causing the actual disease, prompting the immune system to generate specific antibodies and long-lived memory B and T cells. If the actual live pathogen attempts to infect the body in the future, these memory cells instantly recognize the invader and launch a massive, rapid, and highly effective secondary immune response to neutralize it before the disease can develop.

Advantage 1: It is highly useful for detecting genetic abnormalities or chromosomal disorders like Down syndrome.
Advantage 2: It helps determine the survivability of the fetus and detect severe metabolic disorders.

questions.solution:
Amniocentesis is an advanced prenatal diagnostic procedure wherein a doctor uses a specialized surgical needle to carefully extract a small sample of the amniotic fluid directly from the uterus surrounding the developing fetus. This fluid contains shed fetal cells and dissolved substances which are then cultured and analyzed in a laboratory. 
The two major medical advantages of this technique are: First, it allows for the highly accurate early detection of severe genetic abnormalities or chromosomal disorders, such as Down syndrome or Klinefelter's syndrome. Second, it can be used to thoroughly test for specific life-threatening metabolic disorders and assess overall fetal survivability before birth.

(b) 3 amino acids will be formed. The fourth codon becomes UGA, which is a stop codon.

questions.solution:
(a) The given mRNA consists of exactly 8 consecutive triplet codons without any terminating stop codon at the end. If the substitution of 'U' by 'C' selectively occurs in the 5th codon (UUC), it directly transforms into CUC. Because CUC is a perfectly valid sense codon that specifies a standard amino acid, the ongoing translation process will continue completely unimpeded, resulting in a full polypeptide chain comprising exactly 8 amino acids.
(b) If the fourth codon (CGA) has its 'C' suddenly substituted by a 'U', the resulting sequence transforms instantly into UGA. UGA serves universally as a 'Stop' or terminator codon during translation. Thus, the ribosome will immediately halt polypeptide synthesis exactly at the fourth codon, prematurely releasing a truncated polypeptide chain consisting of only the preceding 3 amino acids.

questions.text_english:
With reference to the set-ups (A, B and C) given below, of the electrophoretic separation of a mixture of DNA fragments of varied lengths, answer the questions that follow:
(a) In which one of the two Set-ups, A or B, would you see the DNA fragments separated and why? Justify your answer.
(b) In Set-up C, which one of the two, I/II, are the bands of longer fragments of DNA? Justify your answer.

key_points: (a) Set-up A. DNA fragments are negatively charged and move towards the positive electrode (anode).
(b) Band I. Longer fragments face more resistance from the agarose gel matrix and travel slower, staying closer to the well.

questions.solution:
(a) We would successfully observe the DNA fragments separating in Set-up A. This is because DNA fragments are inherently negatively charged molecules due to their phosphate groups. When placed under a strong electric field in gel electrophoresis, they must be loaded near the negative electrode (cathode) so they are strongly repelled and naturally forced to migrate downwards towards the positive electrode (anode). In Set-up B, loading them directly at the anode would simply prevent any forward migration into the gel entirely.
(b) In Set-up C, the visible bands grouped under region 'I' absolutely represent the significantly longer and larger fragments of DNA. According to the molecular sieving effect of the agarose gel matrix, the rate of migration is strictly inversely proportional to the physical size of the DNA fragment. Therefore, the bulkier, longer fragments face much more physical resistance, travel significantly slower through the pores, and consequently remain positioned much closer to the loading well at the top compared to the smaller, lighter fragments in region II.

questions.text_english:
Three crosses were carried out in pea plants with respect to flower colour violet/white (V/v) and flower position axial/terminal (A/a). Study in the table the crosses 'a', 'b' and 'c' where parental phenotypes and their F1 progeny phenotypes are given.

Parental plants (Phenotypes) | F1 Progeny (Phenotypes)
(a) Violet, axial × white, axial | 6/16 white, axial, 2/16 white, terminal, 6/16 violet, axial, 2/16 violet, terminal (actually the pdf says violet, axial twice, I will infer standard ratio)
(b) Violet, axial × white, terminal | 1/4 violet, axial, 1/4 violet, terminal, 1/4 white, axial, 1/4 white, terminal
(c) Violet, axial × violet, axial | 3/4 violet, axial, 1/4 white, axial

Find the genotypes of each of the parental pairs of crosses 'a', 'b' and 'c'.

key_points: Cross (a): VvAa x vvAa
Cross (b): VvAa x vvaa
Cross (c): VvAA x VvAA (or VvAa x VvAA depending on assumption, VvAA x VvAA yields 100% axial)

questions.solution:
To perfectly determine the correct parental genotypes, we must independently and rigorously analyze the segregation of each distinct trait in the F1 progeny.
For cross (a): The given parental phenotype is Violet, axial × White, axial. The F1 progeny displays both Violet and White precisely in a 1:1 ratio (indicating Vv × vv), while the Axial to Terminal ratio is exactly 3:1 (indicating Aa × Aa). Therefore, combining these, the accurate parental genotypes for cross (a) are VvAa and vvAa.
For cross (b): The given phenotype is Violet, axial × White, terminal. The F1 progeny distinctly shows a perfect standard test cross ratio of 1:1:1:1 for all four phenotypic combinations. This mathematically proves the Violet, axial parent is fully heterozygous for both traits, and the White, terminal parent is fully homozygous recessive. Therefore, the exact genotypes are VvAa and vvaa.
For cross (c): The phenotype is Violet, axial × Violet, axial. The F1 progeny clearly shows segregation for flower colour (Violet to White is 3:1, firmly indicating both parents are heterozygous Vv × Vv) but absolute 100% uniformity for flower position (all are axial, meaning no recessive 'a' alleles combined, so at least one parent must be completely homozygous AA). Thus, the parental genotypes can be definitively stated as VvAA and VvAa (or both VvAA).

questions.text_english:
(a) Mention the advantages of 'ART'.
(b) Explain the 'ICSI' and 'AI' methods of assisted reproductive technologies.

key_points: (a) ART (Assisted Reproductive Technologies) helps infertile couples to have children through advanced medical procedures.
(b) ICSI (Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection) is a specialized procedure where a single healthy sperm is directly injected into the ovum to form an embryo in the laboratory.
AI (Artificial Insemination) is a technique where semen collected from the husband or a donor is artificially introduced into the vagina or the uterus of the female.

questions.solution:
(a) The primary and most significant advantage of ART (Assisted Reproductive Technologies) is that it provides highly advanced medical solutions and procedures that enable infertile couples, who are otherwise biologically unable to conceive naturally, to successfully have children and experience parenthood.
(b) ICSI and AI are two vital clinical procedures under ART.
ICSI stands for Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection. This is a highly specialized and precise laboratory procedure used primarily to treat severe male infertility. In this method, a single, carefully selected healthy sperm is physically injected directly into the cytoplasm of the harvested ovum using micro-needles to forcefully ensure fertilization and embryo formation in-vitro.
AI stands for Artificial Insemination. This effective technique is utilized when the male partner has an extremely low sperm count or is physically unable to inseminate. Healthy semen collected from either the husband or a matching donor is artificially and carefully introduced directly into the vagina or directly into the uterus (IUI) of the female to assist natural fertilization inside her body.

questions.text_english:
(a) Give the scientific name of the bacteria widely used in biotechnology to create a GM cotton crop resistant to bollworm attacks.
(b) Explain how GM cotton crop is able to resist insect attacks.

key_points: (a) Bacillus thuringiensis.
(b) The GM cotton expresses the 'cry' genes (cryIAc, cryIIAb) which produce inactive toxic protein crystals.

questions.solution:
(a) The exact scientific name of the beneficial soil bacterium widely utilized in modern biotechnology to successfully create bollworm-resistant Genetically Modified (GM) cotton is Bacillus thuringiensis.
(b) The GM cotton crop (commonly and commercially known as Bt Cotton) successfully resists catastrophic insect attacks by heavily relying on specific lethal genes (like cryIAc and cryIIAb) isolated directly from the Bacillus thuringiensis bacteria. These specialized genes are intricately incorporated into the plant's genome, prompting the plant tissues to constantly produce highly specific insecticidal protein crystals. Inside the plant, these toxic proteins remain safely in a completely inactive protoxin state. However, when an attacking bollworm ingests the plant's tissues, the highly alkaline pH environment inside the insect's gut rapidly solubilizes the robust crystals, instantly converting the protoxin into an active deadly toxin. This newly activated toxin firmly binds to the surface of the midgut epithelial cells of the insect, rapidly creating massive pores. This devastating cellular disruption causes violent swelling and massive cell lysis, leading to the immediate starvation and subsequent death of the attacking pest.

questions.text_english: Describe the mutualistic relationship that exists between the Mediterranean orchid Ophrys and a bee species.

key_points: The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys employs a strategy called 'sexual deceit' to guarantee pollination.
One petal of the orchid flower bears an uncanny resemblance to the female of the bee species in size, colour, and markings.
The male bee is strongly attracted to the flower, mistaking it for a female, and attempts to 'pseudocopulate' with it.
During this process, pollen is dusted onto the male bee. When the bee performs pseudocopulation on another flower, it transfers the pollen, successfully pollinating the orchid.

questions.solution:
The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys exhibits one of the most fascinating examples of co-evolution and mutualistic relationship by employing a highly deceptive strategy known as 'sexual deceit' to guarantee its pollination. 
One specific petal of the Ophrys flower has uniquely evolved to bear an uncanny and perfect resemblance to the female of a particular bee species in terms of its exact size, distinct colouration, and detailed markings. The male bee is incredibly strongly attracted to what it completely misidentifies as a receptive female. Driven by instinct, the male bee lands on the petal and actively attempts to mate with the flower, a process scientifically termed 'pseudocopulation'. 
During this vigorous but futile mating attempt, the sticky pollen grains from the flower's anthers are generously dusted onto the hairy body of the male bee. Disappointed, the bee eventually flies away. When this same pollen-dusted male bee inevitably repeats the pseudocopulation process with another deceptive Ophrys flower, he inadvertently but effectively transfers the pollen to the new flower's stigma. Thus, the orchid achieves highly specific cross-pollination without offering any nectar reward.

इस ऑर्किड के पुष्प की एक पंखुड़ी आकार, विशिष्ट रंग और चिह्नों में एक विशेष प्रजाति की मादा मक्षिका (मधुमक्खी) के समान दिखाई देती है। नर मक्षिका इस फूल को एक असली मादा समझकर उसकी ओर बहुत तेजी से आकर्षित होता है। अपनी वृत्ति से प्रेरित होकर, नर फूल के साथ मैथुन करने का प्रयास करता है, इस जैविक प्रक्रिया को 'कूटमैथुन' (pseudocopulation) कहा जाता है।
इस निरर्थक प्रयास के दौरान, फूल के चिपचिपे परागकण नर मक्षिका के शरीर पर अच्छी तरह चिपक जाते हैं। जब यही परागकणों से सना हुआ नर किसी दूसरे ऑफ्रिस पुष्प के साथ फिर से कूटमैथुन करने का प्रयास करता है, तो उसके शरीर पर लगे परागकण दूसरे फूल के वर्तिकाग्र पर स्थानांतरित हो जाते हैं। इस प्रकार, कोई भी मकरंद (nectar) दिए बिना, ऑर्किड अत्यंत सफलतापूर्वक अपना परागण पूरा कर लेता है।

questions.text_english:
A population of snakes lived in a desert with brown sand. Study the drawings given below showing the change in the population from 'one' to 'two' over time and answer the question that follows. Brown snakes and Grey snakes are represented by alleles A/a (Dominant/recessive).
(a) If the frequency of the recessive trait is 9% in population-one, work out the frequency of homozygous dominant and heterozygous dominant snakes.
(b) Name the mechanism of evolution that must have operated so that population-two evolved from population-one.

key_points: (a) Recessive trait (q^2) = 0.09. So q = 0.3. p = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7. Homozygous dominant (p^2) = 0.49 or 49%. Heterozygous dominant (2pq) = 2(0.7)(0.3) = 0.42 or 42%.
(b) Natural Selection (specifically directional selection caused by predation from migrating birds).

questions.solution:
(a) According to the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium equation, the frequency of the recessive trait (grey snakes, genotype aa) is mathematically represented by q² = 9% or 0.09. Therefore, the frequency of the recessive allele 'a' (represented by q) is the square root of 0.09, which is 0.3. 
Since p + q = 1, the frequency of the dominant allele 'A' (represented by p) is 1 - 0.3 = 0.7.
The frequency of homozygous dominant snakes (AA) is calculated as p² = (0.7)² = 0.49, or 49%.
The frequency of heterozygous dominant snakes (Aa) is calculated as 2pq = 2 * (0.7) * (0.3) = 0.42, or 42%.
(b) The precise evolutionary mechanism observed operating from population-one to population-two is Natural Selection. The migratory birds act as a strong selective pressure by visually preying on the more conspicuous grey snakes against the brown sand, actively leaving the better-camouflaged brown snakes to survive and freely reproduce.

सूत्र p + q = 1 के अनुसार, प्रभावी एलील (p) की आवृत्ति = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7 होगी।
समयुग्मजी प्रभावी साँपों (AA) की आवृत्ति p² = (0.7)² = 0.49 या 49% होगी।
विषमयुग्मजी प्रभावी साँपों (Aa) की आवृत्ति 2pq = 2 × 0.7 × 0.3 = 0.42 या 42% होगी।
(ख) समष्टि-एक से समष्टि-दो के विकास का मुख्य कारण 'प्राकृतिक वरण' (Natural Selection) है। चित्र में प्रवासी पक्षी शिकारियों के रूप में दिखाई दे रहे हैं, जो भूरी रेत पर स्पष्ट दिखने वाले धूसर साँपों का शिकार कर लेते हैं, जिससे वातावरण के अनुकूल छलावरण वाले भूरे साँप बच जाते हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसी एक प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए:
questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following:

sub_questions.text:
(i) प्लाज़्मोडियम के मानव शरीर में प्रविष्ट होने के बाद से संक्रमित व्यक्ति को मादा ऐनोफेलीज़ मच्छर द्वारा काटे जाने तक की अवधि में प्लाज्मोडियम के जीवन चक्र का वर्णन कीजिए ।
(ii) प्लाज़्मोडियम के जीवन चक्र में मादा ऐनोफेलीज़ के शरीर में सम्पन्न होने वाली दो परिघटनाओं का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Describe the life cycle of Plasmodium from the time it enters the human body till a female Anopheles mosquito bites an infected person.
(ii) Mention the two events of Plasmodium life cycle that occur within the female Anopheles body.

key_points: (i) Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites through mosquito bites. They reach the liver, multiply asexually, and burst liver cells.
They then attack Red Blood Cells (RBCs), multiply asexually, and repeatedly rupture RBCs, releasing toxic haemozoin.
Some parasites differentiate into sexual stages (male and female gametocytes) inside the RBCs.
(ii) Inside the mosquito: Fertilization and development occur in the mosquito's gut.
Mature, infective sporozoites subsequently migrate to and are stored in the mosquito's salivary glands.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The complex life cycle of the malaria parasite Plasmodium begins when an infected female Anopheles mosquito bites a healthy human, directly injecting the infective forms called sporozoites into the bloodstream. These sporozoites swiftly travel to the liver, where they aggressively multiply asexually inside the liver cells. Eventually, the bloated liver cells burst, releasing the parasites back into the blood. The parasites then relentlessly attack the Red Blood Cells (RBCs), where they again multiply asexually, causing a vicious cycle of RBC rupture. The continuous rupturing of RBCs releases a highly toxic substance called haemozoin, which reliably triggers the characteristic recurring chills and high fever. Eventually, some of these multiplying parasites inside the RBCs cease asexual division and deliberately differentiate into sexual stages, developing into mature male and female gametocytes. The parasite remains safely in this gametocyte stage in the human blood until another female Anopheles mosquito bites the infected person and ingests them during a blood meal.
(ii) Following the ingestion of the gametocytes, two critical events occur exclusively within the body of the female Anopheles mosquito. First, the male and female gametes fuse (fertilization) and undergo further complex development entirely within the mosquito's intestinal gut. Second, the resulting mature, highly infective sporozoites actively migrate away from the gut and take up residence in the mosquito's salivary glands, patiently waiting to be injected into a new human host.

sub_questions.text:
(i) सुदम अर्बुद तथा दुर्दम अर्बुद के बीच दो अंतर लिखिए ।
(ii) कैंसर के अभिज्ञान हेतु किन्हीं तीन निदानात्मक तकनीकों की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Write two differences between malignant tumor and benign tumor.
(ii) Explain any three diagnostic techniques for the detection of cancer.

key_points: (i) Benign tumors remain confined to their original location, whereas malignant tumors exhibit metastasis, aggressively invading and spreading to surrounding healthy tissues.
Benign tumors grow relatively slowly and cause little damage, while malignant tumors grow rapidly and are extremely lethal.
(ii) Biopsy and Histopathological studies: A small tissue sample is physically excised, stained, and examined under a microscope by a pathologist to identify cancerous cells.
Radiography (X-rays) or CT scans: Uses X-rays to generate 2D or 3D images of the internal organs to detect abnormal masses.
Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): Utilizes strong magnetic fields and non-ionizing radiation to highly accurately detect deep pathological and physiological tissue changes.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The two primary biological differences between a benign tumor and a malignant tumor are as follows. Firstly, a benign tumor generally remains strictly confined to its original location in the body, whereas a malignant tumor inherently exhibits a dangerous property called metastasis, aggressively spreading to distant sites via blood and establishing new tumors. Secondly, a benign tumor grows relatively slowly and causes only localized, minimal damage to the body, whereas a malignant tumor grows incredibly rapidly, invades and destroys surrounding healthy tissues, and proves highly lethal by violently starving normal cells of their essential nutrients.
(ii) The early and accurate detection of cancer critically relies on several highly advanced diagnostic techniques. Three prominent methods include:
1. Biopsy and Histopathological studies: In this highly reliable physical procedure, a small piece of the suspected tissue is surgically extracted, thinly sectioned, chemically stained, and meticulously examined under a high-power microscope by an expert pathologist to distinctly identify abnormal cell division patterns.
2. Computed Tomography (CT) Scans: This advanced radiological technique uses multiple precise X-rays to instantly generate a detailed, computer-rendered three-dimensional image of the internal organs, easily highlighting the exact location and size of any hidden abnormal tissue masses.
3. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): This extremely safe and highly sophisticated technique utilizes powerful magnetic fields and non-ionizing radio frequencies. It is exceptionally accurate at actively detecting both pathological and minute physiological changes within deep living tissues without ever exposing the patient to harmful radiation.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसी एक प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए:
questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following:

sub_questions.text:
(i) परपरागण को प्रोत्साहित करने हेतु पुष्पी पौधों द्वारा विकसित किन्हीं चार युक्तियों की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
(ii) पौधे स्वपरागण को हतोत्साहित क्यों करते हैं ? कोई एक कारण लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Explain any four devices that flowering plants have developed to encourage cross-pollination.
(ii) Why do plants discourage self-pollination? State any one reason.

key_points: (i) Dichogamy: Pollen release and stigma receptivity are not synchronized.
(i) Herkogamy: Physical barriers exist between the anther and stigma.
(i) Self-incompatibility: A genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from germinating or growing down the style.
(i) Dicliny (Unisexuality): Production of strictly unisexual flowers (male and female flowers on different plants).
(ii) Continuous self-pollination eventually leads to inbreeding depression, lowering the evolutionary fitness and vigour of the resulting offspring.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) To aggressively encourage cross-pollination, flowering plants have naturally evolved several ingenious outbreeding devices. Firstly, Dichogamy ensures that pollen release and stigma receptivity are deliberately not synchronized; the anther may mature much earlier than the stigma, or vice versa, preventing autogamy. Secondly, Herkogamy involves specific morphological adaptations where the anther and stigma are placed at drastically different positions or separated by physical barriers, making self-contact impossible. Thirdly, Self-incompatibility serves as a sophisticated genetic mechanism wherein the pistil actively rejects pollen from the exact same plant, stopping pollen tube growth in the style. Lastly, Dicliny involves the plant entirely abandoning hermaphroditism by producing exclusively unisexual flowers, ensuring that outcrossing is the absolute only reproductive option.
(ii) Plants biologically discourage self-pollination primarily because continuous, multi-generational self-pollination severely reduces genetic diversity. This lack of variation eventually leads to a highly detrimental biological phenomenon known as inbreeding depression, which dangerously lowers the overall survival fitness, yield, and evolutionary vigour of the plant's offspring.

एक सामान्य मानव स्त्री के आर्तव चक्र की अंडाशयी तथा गर्भाशयी प्रावस्थाओं की व्याख्या पीयूष तथा अंडाशयी हॉर्मोनों की भूमिका के साथ निम्नलिखित प्रावस्थाओं के अंतर्गत कीजिए :
(i) पुटकीय प्रावस्था/प्रचुरोद्भव प्रावस्था
(ii) स्रावी प्रावस्था
(iii) आर्तव प्रावस्था
sub_questions.text_english:
Explain the ovarian and uterine events taking place along with the role of pituitary and ovarian hormones, during menstrual cycle in a normal human female under the following phases:
(i) Follicular phase/proliferative phase
(ii) Luteal phase/secretory phase
(iii) Menstrual phase

key_points: Follicular phase: Pituitary FSH and LH stimulate primary follicles to mature into Graafian follicles. Growing follicles secrete estrogen, which proliferates the uterine endometrium.

Luteal phase: Following ovulation (caused by LH surge), the ruptured follicle turns into the corpus luteum, which secretes massive amounts of progesterone to thicken and maintain the secretory endometrium for possible implantation.

Menstrual phase: If no fertilization occurs, the corpus luteum degenerates, severely dropping progesterone and estrogen levels. This causes the thickened endometrium to break down and shed as menstrual flow.

sub_questions.solution:
The menstrual cycle in a healthy human female is a highly orchestrated interplay of ovarian and uterine events, driven entirely by pituitary and ovarian hormones.
(i) Follicular phase (Proliferative phase): During this stage, the gradual increase in pituitary gonadotropins (FSH and LH) directly stimulates primary ovarian follicles to grow and mature into a fully developed Graafian follicle. Simultaneously, these growing follicles actively secrete the ovarian hormone estrogen. Surging estrogen levels command the highly vascularized endometrium of the uterus to proliferate and rapidly regenerate itself.
(ii) Luteal phase (Secretory phase): Triggered by a massive LH surge around day 14, ovulation occurs. The remaining ruptured Graafian follicle transforms into a temporary endocrine structure called the corpus luteum. The corpus luteum immediately begins secreting massive quantities of progesterone. Progesterone is utterly essential during this phase as it heavily thickens and robustly maintains the highly secretory endometrial lining, preparing it for the potential implantation of a fertilized ovum.
(iii) Menstrual phase: If fertilization fails to occur, the unutilized corpus luteum inevitably degenerates. Consequently, the bodily levels of progesterone and estrogen plummet drastically. Deprived of hormonal support, the heavily thickened uterine endometrium collapses and breaks down, shedding its blood vessels and tissues out through the vagina as menstrual flow, thus marking the start of a new cycle.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसी एक प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए:
questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following:

sub_questions.text: “विषमयुग्मजी अवस्था में दोनों एलीलों के प्रभाव की स्पष्ट अभिव्यक्ति सहप्रभाविता (कोडोमिनेंस) में परिलक्षित होती है ।” मानव रुधिर वर्ग ABO की वंशागति की सहायता से कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: "The influence of both the alleles in a heterozygous state is clearly expressed in codominance." Explain with the help of inheritance of ABO blood group in humans.

key_points: Codominance is a genetic phenomenon where both alleles in a heterozygote fully express themselves simultaneously without blending.
ABO blood grouping is controlled by the I gene, which has three distinct alleles: IA, IB, and i.
Alleles IA and IB produce slightly different forms of sugar polymers on the RBC surface, whereas allele i does not produce any.
When a person inherits both IA and IB alleles (genotype IAIB), both alleles express their respective sugars fully.
As a result, the RBCs have both A and B types of sugars, determining the individual's blood group as AB, which is a perfect textbook example of codominance.

sub_questions.solution:
Codominance is a unique genetic phenomenon where two distinct alleles of a single gene, when present together in a heterozygous condition, do not exhibit a dominant-recessive relationship but instead express themselves fully and independently. 
The inheritance of the ABO blood group in humans serves as a spectacular example to explain this. The ABO blood groups are rigorously controlled by the 'I' gene, which possesses three multiple alleles: IA, IB, and i. The functional alleles IA and IB direct the synthesis of slightly different forms of antigenic sugar polymers on the plasma membrane of red blood cells (RBCs), whereas the recessive 'i' allele fails to produce any functional sugar. 
When a human offspring inherits the IA allele from one parent and the IB allele from the other parent, their genetic makeup becomes the heterozygous IAIB. In this specific scenario, neither allele masks the other. Instead, because of codominance, both the IA and IB alleles perfectly express their own specific sugars simultaneously. Consequently, the surface of the individual's RBCs gets coated with both A and B types of sugars, resulting in the distinct 'AB' blood group phenotype. This unequivocally proves that both alleles clearly express their individual influences without any blending.

sub_questions.text:
“लैक प्रचालेक (लैक-ओपेरॉन) में जीनों के एक समूह का नियमन तथा अभिव्यक्ति एक साथ एक इकाई के रूप में होता है।”
(i) लैक ओपेरॉन में संरचनात्मक जीनों की सक्रियता के 'आरंभन (स्विचिंग ऑन)' की कार्यविधि (प्रणाली) की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
(ii) “लैक प्रचालेक' के नियमन को ऋणात्मक नियमन कहा जाता है ।” कारण का उल्लेख करते हुए कथन की न्यायसंगतता (औचित्य) सिद्ध कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
"A group of genes are regulated and expressed together as a unit in lac operon."
(i) Explain the mechanism of switching 'on' of the structural genes of lac operon.
(ii) "Regulation of lac operon' is referred to be negatively regulated." Justify giving a reason.

key_points: (i) Lactose acts as an inducer. When lactose is present, it physically binds to the repressor protein produced by the i-gene.
This binding alters the shape of the repressor, making it inactive and preventing it from binding to the operator region.
RNA polymerase then freely binds to the promoter and transcribes the structural genes (z, y, a) into lac mRNA.
(ii) It is termed 'negatively regulated' because the operon is fundamentally kept in a suppressed (switched off) state by the active repressor protein continuously produced by the regulatory gene.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The lac operon is an inducible operon that remains switched off under normal conditions. It is successfully switched 'on' only when its substrate, lactose (or allolactose), is introduced into the bacterial medium. Lactose acts as an inducer. Inside the cell, the regulatory i-gene continuously synthesizes an active repressor protein. The inducer (lactose) physically binds to this active repressor protein, causing a conformational change that renders the repressor entirely inactive. Because the repressor is now disabled, it completely fails to bind to the specific operator region of the operon. With the operator site clear, the RNA polymerase enzyme can easily bind to the promoter site and smoothly initiate the transcription of the three downstream structural genes (z, y, and a) into a single polycistronic mRNA, effectively switching 'on' the operon.
(ii) The physiological regulation of the lac operon by the repressor protein is rigorously referred to as 'negative regulation'. This specific terminology is thoroughly justified because the natural, default state of the repressor protein is actively inhibitory. The repressor continuously binds to the operator sequence and creates a physical blockade, thereby strongly preventing RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon. Thus, the primary control mechanism heavily relies on actively 'stopping' or repressing gene expression.
